text: Now let's read a real file — the actual NYC Taxi trip data, in PySpark.
This is the same file format Lesson 22 read with Pandas' read underscore csv. The call shape looks almost identical, and that's deliberate — Spark wants the jump from Pandas to feel familiar.
Header equals true tells Spark to use the file's real first row as column names — VendorID, pickup time, fare amount — instead of naming every column underscore c-zero, underscore c-one, and so on.

And infer schema equals true has a real cost: Spark reads the file twice — once just to guess the types, once to actually load it. On a large file, that's measurable, which is why production pipelines often pass an explicit schema instead — that's exactly what Lesson 43 covers.
Header for real column names, infer schema for real types — at a real cost. Next lesson: reading JSON, the same API, a different format.
